title: OpenHistory
brief: Turns your Mac activity into a private timeline for you and your AI — local activity history as agent context. Privacy-sensitive by nature; the "private" claim is unverified.
caveat: Privacy-sensitive by nature; the "private" claim is unverified.
details: OpenHistory (openhistory.sh) — an open-source, local-first Mac app that turns your activity into "a private timeline for you & your AI." It observes foreground apps and the macOS Accessibility context you permit (window names, document context, browser domains, visible interface text) — no screenshots, audio, camera, keystrokes, passwords, or private browsing — and summarizes the day into a timeline of completed work, decisions, and unfinished work. Privacy posture is explicit: everything stored in a permission-restricted local directory, no analytics/telemetry, on-device summaries via Apple on-device models or fully off; cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Kimi) are opt-in with your own key and an approved disclosure. Approved local agents (ChatGPT Desktop, Claude Cowork, any local-MCP agent) get a redacted, read-only view through an authenticated MCP server running only on your Mac. Pause at any time, exclude apps, and "delete all local data" wipes everything. Requires macOS 14+.
